title: Phased feature-flip timeline and annotated release notes (May 2026) - draft
content:
Context
This doc is a working draft for a phased feature-flip (also referred to as feature gate flip) for the new routing policy and cache-prefetch behavior landing in serving-runtime and routing components. Goal: reduce risk by staged ramp with explicit verification gates and an annotated release notes section that product/CS can iterate on for customer communication.

High-level cadence (All times PT)
- Week A (canary): May 18 03:00 - May 19 22:00 — limited to 2% traffic in us-west, baseline SLO monitoring only.
- Week B (ramp): May 20 02:00 - May 23 18:00 — 10% -> 25% -> 50% at controlled steps, added synthetic load tests.
- Week C (wide): May 24 01:00 - May 25 23:00 — 75% -> 100% in primary regions, replication to eu-west begins after 95% stable.
- Post-rollout verification window: May 25 23:00 - May 27 23:59 — monitoring, client-telemetry review, open rollback window until May 27 23:59.

Owners and on-call
- Release lead: Avery Chen (release coordination + final rollback authority).
- Runtime owner: Marcus Rivera (serving-runtime changes).
- Routing & infra owner: Nisha Patel.
- SRE verification: Eloise Martin.
- Pager/Ops: primary on-call per rotation.

Pre-cutover checklist (to complete at least 48h before canary)
- [ ] Merge blockers cleared and smoke-tested on staging (PR #789 merged to main).
- [ ] All RI tickets linked: RI-4521 (routing policy), RI-4573 (cache prefetch tuning).
- [ ] Rollout config baked and stored in ConfigRepo (tagged: rollout/featureflip-2026-05-18).
- [ ] Release notes draft prepared and shared with PM/CS (this doc).
- [ ] Backfill synthetic tests for tail latency and token throughput in test harness.
- [ ] Canary key set and canary service account credentials rotated.
- [ ] Capacity check: reserved dedicated pools available for emergency burst (contact: infra-billing@s.redwood.ai).

Canary window runbook (May 18)
- Step 0: Announce start on #release-ops and send to #eng-all.
- Step 1: Deploy routing binary to canary hosts (2 instances per AZ) and enable feature gate = true for tag canary-2pct.
- Step 2: Warmup: run 10m of synthetic requests across rate-limited traffic to populate caches.
- Step 3: Verify health endpoints (10x): /health, /ready, /cache-stats.
- Step 4: Baseline SLO checks (first 30m) — if p99 latency increases > 20% vs baseline or error rate > 0.5% absolute, abort.
- Step 5: SRE to run manual A/B queries: known prompts in prompt-regression set (linked: Confluence page).

Ramp plan (safety gates at each step)
- 10% (May 20 02:00) -> wait 90m -> verification metrics stable for 45m -> proceed.
- 25% -> wait 2h -> synthetic load run for 30m -> verification.
- 50% -> wait 4h -> check ingestion and KV cache hit ratio; ensure no spike in token emission or billing anomalies.
- 75% -> internal only (product beta) -> monitor client errors and misrouting.
- 100% -> final promotion; begin eu-west rollout only after 95% stability for 6h.

Abort & rollback criteria (decision tree)
- Immediate rollback triggers (operator should rollback without exec committee):
  - sustained p95/p99 latency regression exceeding 25% for >30m.
  - error rate jump >1.0% absolute for any API that serves production traffic.
  - KV cache corruption or cache key mismatch detected in logs (pattern: cache-miss peak >15% baseline).
- Soft-fail indicators (requires SRE + runtime owner sign-off to continue or pause):
  - small increase in tail latency (10-25%) with explainable cause (e.g., background compaction).
  - isolated region blips (<10% users) where degraded metrics localize.
- Rollback steps (if triggered):
  1) Flip feature gate = false in rollout config and push to all routers.
  2) Scale routing workers to pre-rollout size if autoscale triggered down.
  3) Run integrity checks and issue a hotfix PR if one-off corruption found.
  4) Notify customers and stakeholders via status.redwood.ai and #release-ops.

Post-cutover verification tasks (first 48h)
- [ ] Run full prompt-regression suite twice daily and record diffs.
- [ ] Verify billing delta is within projected cost-savings threshold (Optimize team).
- [ ] Check trace samples for 1% of requests to validate KV cache hits and routing path.
- [ ] Product signoff: PM to confirm no functional regressions in customer flows.
- [ ] CS to review top 10 enterprise customers for anomalies and reach out proactively if needed.

Annotated release notes (DRAFT)
- Feature headline: Improved routing policy + cache prefetch for lower cold-start latency and improved throughput.
- Short description (customer-facing): We are rolling out improvements to how requests are routed to model variants and how model KV cache prefetching reduces cold-start latency. This should reduce tail latency for multi-turn chat and decrease token-level cost for large-batch workloads.
- Technical details (internal):
  - New routing policy performs cost-aware bin packing to prefer hot-model replicas while maintaining latency SLOs.
  - Cache prefetch heuristics now warm consecutive sequence prefixes for active sessions to reduce KV miss rate.
  - Backwards-compatible: clients not impacted unless using internal routing hints.
- Known limitations (to call out):
  - Some multi-tenant edge cases in eu-west may see increased cross-tenant cache pressure — monitoring enabled and limited rollout in eu-west.
  - Edge case: clients using manual routing hints may need to drop hints to benefit from improved packing.
- Developer notes for integrators: Update SDK to at least 1.3.2 to surface routing diagnostics. SDK link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/releases/tag/v1.3.2

Communications plan
- Pre-rollout: brief to customer-success and product outreach team including draft notes and FAQ (send by EOD May 17).
- During rollout: short status pings every major step to #release-ops.
- Post-rollout: release notes sent to customers with opt-in for private postmortem if they see anomalies.

Outstanding risks and blockers
- Risk: subtle mismatch between feature gate config across regions. Mitigation: verifier script to assert config parity (runbook script: scripts/check-config-parity.sh).
- Blocker: one remaining flaky test RI-4599 that occasionally spikes p99 in staging; scheduled fix ETA May 15. Want green before canary.
- Ops question: do we want automatic rollback on billing delta > +30% in first 24h? Need exec signoff.

Open questions for PM/Leadership
- Confirm customer communication cadence: immediate post-100% or staggered? (PM suggestion: staggered + targeted note to top 20 customers).
- Approve emergency burst budget for Dedicated pools (cost center 3-Infra).

Quick links and runbook snippets
- Verifier script: git+ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tools.git//scripts/check-config-parity.sh
- Prompt regression harness: https://ci.redwood.ai/prompt-regressions/builds/series-202605
- Slack: #release-ops, #sre-pager, #product-hosted-api

Notes-to-self / rough items to tidy before finalization
- Move the annotated release notes into the product one-pager and shorten for customer email.
- Attach consolidated metric graphs (p99/p95/error-rate) after each step — currently placeholders.
- Add a small table mapping JIRA tickets -> owner -> verification steps (will add in next revision).

Appendix: quick timeline summary
- May 15: freeze for rollout blockers (code freeze on main for runtime changes).
- May 18: canary 2% us-west.
- May 20-23: controlled ramp to 50%.
- May 24-25: 75% -> 100% and eu-west phased.
- May 27 23:59: rollback window closes unless new opt-in exception granted by release lead.

If you are reading this and have a concern: ping @avery.chen in #release-ops with subject line: "featureflip concern" so we can triage quickly.

-- end of draft --
